runs.name: FreightCar America, Inc.; Nasdaq RAIL, SEC CIK 0001320854, a diversified manufacturer and supplier of railcars and railcar components for bulk commodities and containerized freight primarily in North America from one leased plant in Castanos, Coahuila, Mexico, with rebody, repair, conversion and parts; warrants for 13,619,377 shares exercised by OC III LFE II, LP 2026-06-26, a rights agreement renewed 2026-08-05 and terminated 2026-10-14 under a Stockholder Agreement with the OC III holders, about 48.8%; the FY2025 10-K names no rival and has no Item 1A, Trinity, Greenbrier and National Steel Car (private) taken from the FY2022 10-K as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$5.92** (close of 2026-10-16, Yahoo Finance, aggregator, flagged). Shares **32,791,280** (10-Q cover, `0001193125-26-330623`, checked against 32,775,760 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 and the 8-K of 2026-07-02; the later 8-Ks issue no shares; the $3.57 warrant for 1,636,313 shares left out, about 0.65M on the treasury method, stated); cap **$194.1M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-15). Documents read: the FY2025 10-K (`0001193125-26-098668`, a smaller reporting company with no Item 1A), the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the proxy (`0001213900-26-031465`), the 8-Ks of 2026-07-02, 2026-08-05 and 2026-10-15, the FY2021 to FY2024 10-Ks and the XBRL facts FY2009 to FY2025. Cross-check: FY2025 revenues $500,991 thousand on the filed statement against $501.0M in XBRL and run.py; cash $64,295 thousand likewise. The brief departed in one stated place: the lines of evidence chosen by the analyst from Items 1 and 7. **Q1 IN**: a cyclical railcar assembler selling 78% to financial institutions, the top five customers about 75% of 2025 revenue; the key variables (the delivery cycle, the cost position against the two large builders, the lessors' price) readable from its own and its rivals' filings. **Q2 OUT**: Manufacturing, about 90% of segment profit, decides; a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns: pre-tax operating income on total assets less cash FY2016 to FY2025 averaged -10.9% (operating losses FY2017 to FY2022) against Trinity 4.8% and Greenbrier 9.4%, both with their leasing arms; gross margin 4.0% mean against Greenbrier Manufacturing 13.4% (below in six years of ten, level in three, ahead only in 2023) and Trinity Rail Products operating 6.6%; price first among the bases of competition in the 10-K; the money test failed on the filer's own record (the Castanos capacity stood up in 2019 to 2020 through a joint venture, the partner bought out for $0.2M and 2,257,234 shares); the move to Mexico credited in full reaches only parity with Greenbrier, so OUT and not TOO HARD (NATURE), argued; the field's volume already falling (Trinity rail-products revenue down 41.6% in 2025) and manufacturing gross margin 3.2% in the second quarter of 2026 against 13.4% a year earlier. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop: retained earnings from +$187.5M (2016) to -$220.6M (2024), equity negative 2021 to 2025 and $36.2M at 2026-06-30 after the June 2026 net warrant exercise issued 13,619,377 shares for no cash (about 41.5% of the shares now outstanding); warrants to the lender's affiliate in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023; Series C preferred of $85.4M issued 2023 and redeemed 2024 from a $115.0M term loan, $27.9M of preferred dividends in 2024; term loan $100.7M at 9.7% to 2028-12-31; net debt $37.75M; a $49.0M valuation-allowance release in FY2025 income; warrant fair-value losses $99.5M (2024) and $32.2M (2025). **Integrity facts recorded, not judged**: $24,543,000 paid in 2025 to the family of director Jesus Gil (the plant's lessors, suppliers, trucking, royalties); a rights plan adopted 2026-08-05 and terminated 2026-10-14 under the Stockholder Agreement with the 48.8% holder; featured Adjusted EBITDA and full-year guidance, Adjusted EBITDA 31.67% of the CEO's and CFO's bonus; corporate professional fees up $5.5M in 2025, cause not stated. Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, all capital spending, finance-lease principal and acquisitions; all-equity adds back interest at 21%): FY2021 to FY2025 -55.6, 7.8, -6.2, 38.3, 31.3, literal window mean $3.12M; FY2021 aberrational under specific (a) (the plant move and a $24.7M VAT draw), so the cycle base FY2018 to FY2024, all-equity -$21.09M a year. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value a single no-growth point **-$12.99** a share all-equity (the growth changing sign, specific (b)) against $5.92, literal window $0.96 beside; no case earns the floor (about $22M to $23M a year needed); fair **-$7.58 all-equity** (-$7.31 equity-only; literal window $0.16 and -$0.91); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Checks that are not cases: FY2022 to FY2025 only, 9.1% at the price; FY2024 and FY2025 only, 18.3%. Contamination declared by the analyst: the LZRFY commit subjects, research-folder names in git status (AYI, ARCB), the memory index and one filtered `Test Runs/` listing for the name that returned nothing; none used. Commits a4c7ee23 (template), c8498e80 (Step 0, foundations, standing rule, Q1), 57f5f099 (Q2), 6e861e15 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS; the dispatcher's `_fold_cite_check.py` 35 ids, 22 quoted fragments, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) section C gives two exits (TOO HARD (NATURE) for an untested change for the better, OUT for a field of ordinary returns) for one fact pattern and does not say which governs; (2) specific (a) has no rule for a business that changed its form inside the cycle; (3) the shelter convention's 'run out inside ten years' is ambiguous for federal losses that never expire; (4) the all-equity basis names no tax rate for the interest added back; (5) the brief's rival rule meets a 10-K with no Item 1A and no named rival. Could not get: the price of the second aftermarket acquisition after 2026-06-30; a Trinity segment gross margin (its operating margin used).
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (a railcar builder selling mostly to lessors from one leased plant in Mexico). Manufacturing, about 90% of segment profit, decides: a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns; pre-tax operating income on assets less cash -10.9% mean FY2016 to FY2025 against Trinity 4.8% and Greenbrier 9.4% (rivals from the FY2022 10-K, a CONVENTION of the run), gross margin 4.0% mean against Greenbrier Manufacturing 13.4%, the move to Mexico reaching only parity in 2024 and 2025, price first among the bases of competition, capacity stood up cheaply by the filer itself, and manufacturing gross margin 3.2% in the second quarter of 2026. Facts after the stop: retained earnings from +$187.5M to -$220.6M, equity negative 2021 to 2025, 13.6M shares issued for no cash on the June 2026 warrant exercise, a 9.7% term loan; integrity facts recorded, not judged: $24.5M paid in 2025 to a director's family, a rights plan adopted and terminated under an agreement with the 48.8% holder, featured Adjusted EBITDA in the bonus. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value -$12.99 a share all-equity (single no-growth point, cycle base) against $5.92, no case earning the floor; fair -$7.58 all-equity, -$7.31 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: two exits in section C for one fact pattern, no cycle-base rule for a business that changed form, the shelter wording, no tax rate for the all-equity add-back, a 10-K naming no rival.
